slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: Data Landscapers' 54-country review states that rural primary schools in Angola predominantly record attendance, enrolment and grades on paper, with the data aggregated later into the central EMIS/SIGE at provincial or district level through paper forms or manual entry, and that it found no evidence of direct digital entry in rural schools; the document gives no date for this, so its published date is used.
facts.system: paper school records (no learner-record system at the school)

systems.tiers: provincial and district levels, where school data arriving on paper forms are aggregated or keyed; described as provincial or pilot in scale, not in rural schools

note: Passages file. The one fact is a statement of absence (paper at the school), recorded under the sub-indicator's class with no system behind it; SIGE as described here only receives aggregated school data above the school, so it is class census. The source's own header marks its country rows as an AI-assisted compilation, the author's analysis and not sourced fact.
